idea.body: A square root can often be split apart to make it simpler. When a number under the root has a perfect square factor, pull that factor out as a whole number in front of the root. sqrt(50) is sqrt(25 times 2), and since 25 is a perfect square, this becomes 5 sqrt(2). Two radicals only add or subtract directly when they share the same number under the root. This is much like how 3x and 5x combine but 3x and 5y do not. 5 sqrt(2) plus 2 sqrt(2) is 7 sqrt(2). Multiplying radicals is the reverse of splitting: sqrt(a) times sqrt(b) is sqrt(a times b). A fraction with a root alone in the denominator gets rationalised by multiplying top and bottom by that same root, so 1/sqrt(2) becomes sqrt(2)/2.

steps: sqrt(8) is sqrt(4 times 2), so it simplifies to 2 sqrt(2).
3 sqrt(8) becomes 3 times 2 sqrt(2), which is 6 sqrt(2).
sqrt(18) is sqrt(9 times 2), so it simplifies to 3 sqrt(2).
Both terms now share the same radical: 6 sqrt(2) plus 3 sqrt(2).

ways.name: Pull out the largest square
ways.when: Use this default method whenever a number under the root has a perfect square factor.
steps: Find the largest perfect square factor of 72: it is 36, since 72 = 36 times 2.
Split the root: sqrt(72) = sqrt(36) times sqrt(2).
ways.trap: Splitting off a smaller square factor, like 4, leaving more simplifying still to do.

ways.name: The prime factor pairs
ways.when: Use this when the largest square factor is hard to spot by eye.
steps: Break 200 into prime factors with a tree: 200 = 2 times 2 times 2 times 5 times 5.
Group the primes into pairs: (2, 2) and (5, 5), with one 2 left over.
Each pair sends one factor outside the root: 2 times 5 is 10.
The leftover 2 stays under the root: sqrt(200) = 10 sqrt(2).
ways.trap: Pulling out only one number from a pair instead of moving the whole pair outside.

ways.name: Multiply then simplify
ways.when: Use this when two radicals are multiplied together instead of added.
steps: Multiply what is under each root together: sqrt(6) times sqrt(15) is sqrt(6 times 15).
6 times 15 is 90, so this is sqrt(90).
90 has the perfect square factor 9, since 90 = 9 times 10.
sqrt(90) = sqrt(9) times sqrt(10), which is 3 sqrt(10).
ways.trap: Multiplying the two numbers under the roots but forgetting to simplify what is left.

stretch.prompt: A square's diagonal is 6 sqrt(2) units long. What is the square's area, in square units?
explanation: A square's diagonal is its side length times sqrt(2).
So the side length is 6 units.
The area is 6 times 6, which is 36.
stretch.useAgain: when a square's diagonal is given as a multiple of sqrt(2) and the area is wanted.
hints: Divide the diagonal by sqrt(2) to find the side length.
Once you have the side length, square it for the area.
